column1: # *** THE MONTEVIDEO DISPENSATION REGISTER, SWEPT ON EVERY COMPOUND FORM - FINISHED 12 OCTOBER 2026. ***
# *** THIS FILE WAS PUBLISHED AT MIDDAY ON 12 OCTOBER WITH A FALSE CLAIM OF NOVELTY, CORRECTED TWENTY-SIX MINUTES LATER, AND IS REWRITTEN, NOT DELETED. ***
# It announced as a discovery a mechanism data/compound-surname-sweep.tsv had recorded on 14 September.
# The first row below says so. The rest is what today's work actually adds: five compound forms that
# had never been run, each read to the END of its result set, and a controlled null on a tenth
# METHOD NOTE: FamilySearch's full-text results page takes count=100 in the URL, which turns a
# top-ranked first page into a whole result set. Without it this sweep would have been the same
# ranked-list mistake this archive has already made twice.
*** FIRST, WHAT THIS FILE GOT WRONG ***
column2: published at midday on 12 October as a new finding, corrected twenty-six minutes later
column3: *** THE MECHANISM WAS NOT NEW. THE ARCHIVE FOUND IT ON 14 SEPTEMBER. ***
column4: data/compound-surname-sweep.tsv says it in almost these words: the September sweep's formula was LERENA FELIGRESA *** and the compound surname sits between the two words. *** That file had already run Lerena Juanico, Lerena Lenguas and Lerena Traibel, and had already found the NINTH dispensation through it.
column5: *** SO THE ERRAND THIS FILE WAS WRITTEN AGAINST WAS STALE - the work was partly done and the errand never closed - and this file announced a known mechanism as a discovery. *** It is kept, rewritten, rather than deleted, because an archive that quietly removes its duplicated findings cannot tell how often it duplicates them. See data/corrections.tsv, 12 October.

column1: *** THE NINTH DISPENSATION, WHICH WAS ALREADY HELD ***
column2: full text, "Lerena Juanico", complete result set of 35
column3: *** Arquidiocesis de Montevideo. Marriage Dispensation Records, June 1913 - image ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-P72J-V ***
column4: Found 14 September through the query "Massera" "Lerena", not through a compound form.
column5: *** The petition of JOSE PEDRO MASSERA, 19 June 1913, to marry Dona EMA SIXTA LERENA JUANICO, feligresa de la metropolitana, asking to be dispensed one conciliar proclama. *** Opened again today at the plate. *** Note what the machine transcript does to the groom: it gives Massera once and Tomasera once, in one short document *** - which is the same lesson as /name/, in a Latin alphabet and a modern hand.

column1: *** WHAT TODAY ACTUALLY ADDS: FIVE FORMS NOBODY HAD RUN ***
column2: full text, complete result sets at count=100 - Lerena Pelaez, Lerena Fernandez, Lerena Villademoros, Lerena Cardozo, Lerena Larriera, Lerena Razzetti
column3: *** ONE touches the dispensation register, and it was already held ***
column4: September ran four forms: Lerena Juanico, Lerena Lenguas, Lerena Traibel and Avelino Lerena. The other six had never been run at all.
column5: *** Lerena Cardozo returns Arquidiocesis de Montevideo. Marriage Dispensation Records 1911 *** - the double-first-cousin dispensation this archive already holds in its own file, which makes it a CONTROL rather than a find: the method demonstrably reaches the register. *** Lerena Pelaez (4 volumes), Lerena Fernandez (24), Lerena Villademoros (1), Lerena Larriera (1) and Lerena Razzetti (1) touch it nowhere. ***

column1: *** AND THE RESULT, WHICH IS A NULL WORTH HAVING ***
column2: the eight compound forms together, each read to the END of its result set rather than to the end of its first page
column4: The register has now been searched three ways: by its own formulae in September (eight found), by the compound surname in September (a ninth found), and by every compound form this archive can name, today.
column5: *** Two of the eight forms reach the register and both land on dispensations already held - 1911 through Cardozo, 1913 through Juanico. *** That is the shape of a controlled null: the queries demonstrably hit the target, and there is nothing else in it. *** The errand is closed. *** What would still change it is a compound this archive has not met, which is the standing weakness of every surname-based sweep here.
